issues.claim: "at businesses like yours that gap often means older complaints went unanswered" (audit section 2)
issues.problem: Unsupported generalisation placed immediately after the Birdeye-vs-Yelp rating gap, so it reads as an implied statement about Albany County Fasteners' own complaint history. No cited source says anything about unanswered complaints at this business or at comparable firms, and it is not framed as an inference. It also brushes against the 'implied insider knowledge' / alarmist tone risk: the only sourced complaint evidence is that an aggrieved Yelp reviewer said management would not make good on an issue.
issues.fix: Delete the clause, or restate the sourced fact and frame the risk explicitly as an inference, e.g. "Ratings diverge by platform (4.6 on Birdeye, 2.5 on Yelp from 21 reviews), which suggests older complaints on one channel were never resolved - an inference, not something the company has confirmed." Do not attribute motive or neglect.

issues.claim: "businesses like yours often prepare these by hand through the sales team" (audit section 1)
issues.problem: Presented as a general market fact with no source. Nothing on the B2B quote page, About Us page or FAQs states how quotes are prepared internally (manual or otherwise), so the audit asserts the client's process without evidence. The rest of the sentence (purchasing, fulfilment and marketing each sit with one person) is properly sourced.
issues.fix: Cut the unsourced clause and state only what the site shows, e.g. "You quote listed and unlisted products, custom parts, C of C certificates and MTRs, all handled by your in-house sales team - and purchasing, fulfilment and marketing each sit with one person."

issues.problem: No assumptions are disclosed anywhere in the audit, and the productivity assumption behind the $6,000-$18,000 support range comes from NBER Working Paper 31161 (14% average / 34% for novice agents, 5,179 agents), which does not appear in the audit's Sources list. The audit cites only the two O*NET wage pages. Recomputation: order clerk median $46,270 + ~25% burden, 0.75-1.0 FTE, 40-60% of handling time recovered gives ~$17k-$35k (range 1 holds only if the FTE band is 0.75-1.0, not the 0.5-1.0 in the underlying analysis); CSR median $47,740, 1.5 FTE at 50-60% automatable and 14-34% gain gives ~$6.3k-$18.4k (range 2 holds); $47,740 at 5-14 hrs/week gives ~$7.5k-$20.9k (range 3 holds).
issues.fix: Add a one-line assumption note under each impact figure (volume, minutes per transaction, loaded NJ median wage, share of time recovered) and add the NBER w31161 citation - or drop the impact figures from the audit and keep them for the discovery deck. Also align range 1 with its stated FTE band (or state 0.75-1.0 FTE).

issues.claim: Sources annotation: "B2B quote page - unlisted/custom quotes, C of C/MTR, stock-and-lock, tiered piece/pack/bulk pricing" (also the email's "stock-and-lock programs")
issues.problem: The B2B Request-A-Quote page does not use the term stock-and-lock; it describes "Stock & Release Programs". The phrase "stock and lock pricing" appears on the About Us page instead, so the citation is attached to the wrong page.
issues.fix: Change the annotation to "Stock & Release programs" for the B2B page and cite About Us for "stock and lock pricing"; in the email, use the site's own wording ("stock-and-release" or "stock-and-lock pricing") so the founder recognises it.

issues.claim: Email: "... certificates of conformance and stock-and-lock programs, all handled by your own team out of the Edison warehouse"
issues.problem: Partly inferred. The site confirms an in-house sales team for quotes and certifications, but C of C/MTR can also be self-served at checkout by adding the COC or MTR SKU, and no page states that the sales team works out of the Edison warehouse (the address is the warehouse, so it is a reasonable but unstated inference).
issues.fix: Soften to "quotes on unlisted and custom parts, C of C/MTR paperwork and stock programmes, handled by your own sales team" - keeps every element sourced and avoids the unverifiable 'out of the warehouse' detail.
